title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 'universal case' of the loop-equation analysis in the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. Π is a profinite fundamental group (Π̂ denotes its inner automorphisms). ρ is a distinguished loop, σ an automorphism of order 3 and τ an involution, linked by the relation τ(ρ) = σ(ρ^{-1}). N*_ρ is the group of automorphisms sending ρ to ρ^{±1}, and Z_ρ ⊂ N*_ρ is the subgroup fixing ρ. M[0] = Z^!_{ρ,σ} is a group of automorphisms, M(0) ⊂ M[0] is its index-related subgroup, and M^! is an index-2 'shriek' subgroup. Γ_{ρ,σ} (≅ the Galois-type group Π_Q^~) is a quotient of Z^!_{ρ,σ}. μ = {±1} is a group of order 2.

On the previous page Grothendieck claimed that the canonical homomorphism (130), Γ_{ρ,σ} → N*_ρ/{±1}, does not lift to N*_ρ. Equivalently, the pulled-back μ-extension Γ̃_{ρ,σ} is non-trivial. Via a diagram of cartesian squares (155), he identified this extension with M(0)^~, the μ-extension of M(0) induced from S_0^πΓ^!_{ρ,σ}. The top of this page finishes that identification: through the canonical isomorphism M(0) ≅ Γ_{ρ,σ}, Γ̃ corresponds to M(0)^~, whose non-triviality was 'seen above'.

He then gives a second, more direct construction of both the homomorphism and the extension.
- (146) Set N*!_ρ := N*_ρ ∩ M^!.
- (147) The kernel of N*!_ρ → Γ_{ρ,σ} is N*!_ρ ∩ 𝔖^+ = L_ρ ∩ Π = μ. Here 𝔖^+ is presumably the 'inner/symmetry' subgroup one quotients by.
- (148) The map N*!_ρ → Γ_{ρ,σ} is surjective. It suffices that every u ∈ M(0) is congruent mod 𝔖 to an element of N*!_ρ.

Proof of (148). Write u(ρ) = α(ρ) with α ∈ Π̂_τ = {1,τ}·Π̂.
- If ε_3(u) = 1, then α ∈ Π̂ and α^{-1}u fixes ρ, so α^{-1}u ∈ Z_ρ ⊂ N*_ρ.
- If ε_3(u) = -1, write α = α_0τ with α_0 ∈ Π̂. Then u(ρ) = α_0(τ(ρ)) = α_0(σ(ρ^{-1})), hence (σ^{-1}α_0^{-1}u)(ρ) = ρ^{-1}, so σ^{-1}α_0^{-1}u ∈ N*_ρ.

The next page draws the conclusion. There is an exact sequence 1 → μ → N*!_ρ → Γ_{ρ,σ} → 1, realising Γ̃_{ρ,σ} concretely. The induced map Γ ≅ N*!_ρ/μ → N*_ρ/μ is the homomorphism (130).

The point of all this is to explain the sign ambiguity: the Galois-type group acts on the loop ρ only up to inversion, and this cannot be lifted without passing to a ±1 central extension.
errors: Gap in (148): he checks that σ^{-1}α_0^{-1}u (resp. α^{-1}u) lies in N*_ρ, but not that it lies in M^! as required for N*!_ρ. He also does not check that σ and α_0 lie in 𝔖, which the congruence mod 𝔖 needs. Presumably both are immediate from definitions, but they are unstated.
In (147) the equality L_ρ ∩ Π = μ is asserted without argument on this page; it presumably depends on earlier pages.

The equation numbering is non-monotone: (146)-(148) follow (155) on the previous page, and the next page labels the sequence '(199)'. This suggests renumbering or misreading, not a mathematical error.

ideas.what: Realising the sign-ambiguous action Γ → N*_ρ/{±1} of a Galois-type group on a loop (ρ ↦ ρ^{±1}) via a concrete central μ-extension N*!_ρ = N*_ρ ∩ M^!
ideas.modern_name: pullback/lifting obstruction of a homomorphism to N/{±1}; central extension by μ_2 (dihedral normaliser of a procyclic subgroup)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard group theory; the setting is the Grothendieck–Teichmüller / loop-equation framework (Drinfeld, Ihara, et al.)
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or Longue Marche in this form, as far as I know; unsure

ideas.what: Surjectivity argument by splitting on the sign character ε_3 and using the relation τ(ρ) = σ(ρ^{-1}) to correct an automorphism into the normaliser of ρ
ideas.modern_name: normaliser/centraliser computation for inertia generators under outer automorphisms (S_3-symmetry of P^1 − {0,1,∞})

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine verification inside a long computation. It gives an alternative construction of a ±1 extension already identified on the previous page. Grothendieck himself, on the next page, says he got lost in detours and starts a recapitulation. Nothing here appears new beyond standard group-theoretic bookkeeping.
transcription_corrections: 'M(ω)' throughout should read 'M(0)', consistent with the previous page.
'γ_{ρ,σ}' should be 'Γ_{ρ,σ}'; likewise 'γ_{ρ,σ̃}' should be 'Γ̃_{ρ,σ}' (the tilde is on Γ).
The underbrace in (147) likely reads 'Π_Q^~' (as on the previous page) rather than 'Π_Q^{ab}'.
'Ker(N_ρ^{*!} → Γ_{ρ,σ}) = L_ρ ∩ Π = μ': L_ρ may carry a superscript; it is uncertain.
'... moins qu'elle n'était pas triviale' probably reads 'au moins ... qu'elle n'était pas triviale' or similar.
On the next page, 'Z_ρ^{α!}' is probably 'N_ρ^{*!}'.
